memory_candidates.content: A plan phase declared Verification Tier: full can still be discharged against a cheaper, narrower check when the dispatch file carries a Batch Gate Deferral directive (this task is one of several implement-phase dispatches inside one multi-task /orchestrate batch invocation). The directive sanctions run-all.sh --only SUITE[,...] or verify-deploy.sh --only-gate N[,...] instead of the unscoped complete gate set. Important nuance: --only-gate 8 itself still runs the ENTIRE suite battery (186-193 suites) -- it narrows which numbered GATES run, not which suites WITHIN gate 8 -- so it is not actually cheap, and it internally fails on ANY known-failures.txt roster row since it does not pass --fail-on-new, meaning it can report FAIL for reasons wholly unrelated to the task at hand. The run-all.sh --only SUITE,SUITE,... form is the one that is actually scoped and cheap; prefer it over --only-gate when the directive offers both options.

A gate-lock mutex (specs/.gate-lock) can be left stale-held after a foreground verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh invocation is killed mid-run by an outer `timeout N` wrapper (SIGTERM via exit 143). A subsequent invocation then waits out the full lock-wait window and reports a generic FAIL with no real detail, even though no suite actually failed -- it never got to run. If a verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh call is killed by a timeout wrapper, check specs/.gate-lock and the named holder PID's liveness before retrying; a dead holder with a stale lock file explains an otherwise-confusing immediate-FAIL-after-long-wait on retry.
